objective: Implement the first bounded read-only GitHub public-publisher attestation verifier adapter, using an externally pinned gh executable and trusted root, an exact independently supplied policy digest, artifact/release-pin byte checks, and fail-closed negative tests. This is phase A of PQ-01, not publication, installer enforcement or final production qualification.
nonGoals: No attestation publishing/signing workflow, release, actual adopter install or deployment; no GitHub release/target writes or changes to existing locked installer behavior
No assertion that test/mock CLI output proves real GitHub publisher authenticity; real signature and independently provisioned policy custody require separate PQ-01B live qualification
No verification based only on candidate-authored attestation JSON, signer labels, tool statuses or a release pin; no mandatory second reviewer
No new dependency in the standard factory runtime or private repository entitlement assumptions; no unnecessary CI reruns
decisions: Use a verified external GitHub CLI attestation verifier instead of embedding a new handwritten Sigstore cryptographic verifier in the Python runtime; switch only if offline/private requirements invalidate CLI support

Require independently supplied SHA-256 of a strict, versioned policy; policy binds expected public repo, exact signer workflow and digest, source ref/digest, release artifact digest, verifier binary digest, Sigstore trusted-root bytes/digest, signed-evidence freshness
Verifier runs without inheriting GitHub auth tokens, shell, or caller home, against copied immutable inputs under a private temporary directory, with bounded I/O/time and no target writes
Continue existing SF-13 externally pinned preview API unchanged and unqualified; PQ-01B must integrate effect-boundary installer verification before any production installation claim
Use fixture subprocess/verifier mocks for adapter failure cases; reserve genuine signed attestation acceptance for authorized live qualification

obligations.description: Validate strict policy + release-pin and artifact identity; compare policy SHA to independently supplied expected digest, and verify binary/trusted-root hashes; reject expiry and unsafe symlink/paths.
Call verified GitHub CLI with pinned repo, signer workflow/digest, source ref/digest, bundle and trusted root in offline mode; parse bounded verification output and bind subject SHA.
Reject missing/wrong signer, source, digest, policy, tool/root mismatch, malformed/expired policy, malformed output and execution unavailable/failed; no authentication from fixture strings.

CLI returns read-only cryptographic verifier outcome but no production release/installation authority. Mark live signer/key custody and installer boundary as PQ-01B pending; no legacy fake acceptance.
Verify only declared changed paths, local targeted tests and mandatory exact PR/merge group CI as appropriate; no ad hoc new workflows.

structure: src/sf/publisher.py: fail-closed input/policy/attestation CLI verification boundary, no signer/publisher authority creation
src/sf/cli.py: sf distribution authenticate read-only command, retaining existing build/verify paths
tests/test_publisher.py: independent fake external verifier and negative-case tests with no live network
docs/factory/PQ01_PUBLISHER.md: implementation, trust custody/versions, unqualified live/install boundary
docs/factory/evidence/PQ-01A.md: tests and exact source/gate identity when observed
impact: New separately invoked read-only authenticity adapter; legacy archive/lock and install fixtures untouched
Output is conditional on separately authenticated operator policy and pinned tool/root, and never issues an installation/release grant

budget.network: GitHub current repository operations only; verifier uses offline retained bundle, no external network or credentials
budget.execution: Local focused tests, one native PR run on stable candidate, no repeat unchanged checks; protected queue on separately authorized integration.

externalEffects: No release signing, publication, live attestation verification, target install, production credentials or deployments
Only new task branch/PR in spsoftwarefc/s-f; protect main via normal required checks and queue, no direct merge
